quest.title: Octave of the Maushiro
quest.description: It has been a while since you last contacted Sumida. She said earlier that she would look for some of the other people who took up her commission and conduct an information exchange. Go back to Inazuma and look for her to see how her attempt proceeds.
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x450, Primogem x50, Hero's Wit x5, Mora x50000, Mystic Enhancement Ore x4

dialogues.speaker: Abe
dialogues.text: ...Maybe I just wish that all will go well with him...

dialogues.speaker: Abe
dialogues.text: It's been so long since I've seen him...

dialogues.speaker: Una
dialogues.text: Who knows... Now that I think about it, I pity him.

dialogues.speaker: Una
dialogues.text: Sayo left him behind and left the Sea of Fog. I'm afraid...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Doesn't seem like we can be of any help here...

dialogues.speaker: Ruu
dialogues.text: I wonder how Big Brother Kama's doing...

dialogues.speaker: Una
dialogues.text: Whatever the case, old man, just mind your own mushrooms.

dialogues.speaker: Abe
dialogues.text: Hey now, the Fluorescent Fungi are the good stuff, alright?

dialogues.speaker: Abe
dialogues.text: I'll bring some for you once the ceremony's over.

dialogues.speaker: Una
dialogues.text: Uh, well, much obliged. If not, never mind my eyes, I think my mind might be going too.

dialogues.speaker: Una
dialogues.text: Why, I can barely tell Kito and Kina apart at this point.

dialogues.speaker: Una
dialogues.text: ...Whatever the case, don't concern yourself too much with what happened to the Kama family...

dialogues.speaker: Abe
dialogues.text: I know, I know.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The fog here... really is super thick...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Speaking of which, Paimon wonders what's happening back with Miss Sumida? It seems like she mentioned that she intended to gather all those who took up her commission to meet and discuss some stuff with us...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Well, let's go look for her, {NICKNAME}!

dialogues.speaker: Sango
dialogues.text: Really now, asking me to walk all this way. If this wasn't about "a once-in-a-century find..."

dialogues.speaker: Sumida
dialogues.text: Eh? We've only walked a few steps away from Bantan Sango's storefront, haven't we?

dialogues.speaker: Sango
dialogues.text: It's not a storefront.

dialogues.speaker: Sango
dialogues.text: Bantan Sango is my house of wisdom. The world comes to Bantan Sango, not the other way around.

dialogues.speaker: Ryuuji
dialogues.text: There it is. No. 7 of the lines that President Sango wishes she could say someday.

dialogues.speaker: Ryuuji
dialogues.text: But since cases tend to come to her, she's never had a chance to say it...

dialogues.speaker: Sango
dialogues.text: H—Hey, you don't have to say so much, Ryuuji!

dialogues.speaker: Roald
dialogues.text: *cough* Anyway, regarding Tsurumi Island...

dialogues.speaker: Sumida
dialogues.text: #Ah, you're here. Let me introduce you. This is the renowned {NICKNAME}...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You can, uh, skip the "renowned" bit.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: And Paimon's Paimon!

dialogues.speaker: Roald
dialogues.text: #Ah, so this is the legendary {NICKNAME}...

choices.text: And I'm "legendary" too?

response.speaker: Roald
response.text: Well, your deeds have far surpassed the domain of your average adventurer, that's for sure — indeed, your adventures are what all adventurers' dreams are made of!

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: Right. Let's get to the point. The reason I've asked everyone to gather here is to exchange information about Tsurumi Island.

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: My latest work...

choices.text: Is to unravel the secrets of the island.

response.speaker: Ryuuji
response.text: #It seems that we could count on you after all, {NICKNAME}.

response.speaker: Roald
response.text: Agreed. You certainly do have good judgment, being able to prevent Miss Sumida from going off topic like that.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: (Paimon feels a bit sorry for Miss Sumida...)

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: *whimpers* I'm sorry...

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: Well, to get back to the point, out of all the people affected by incidents related to "Maushiro that should have been found going missing"...

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: I was only able to find the detectives from Bantan Sango and Mr. Roald.

response.speaker: Ryuuji
response.text: It is also true that we were unable to successfully retrieve the Maushiro.

response.speaker: Sango
response.text: Well, I'll solve the mystery for you. Ryuuji must have misplaced it.

response.speaker: Ryuuji
response.text: Not at all. I did lose my way many times after arriving on Tsurumi Island, but I did eventually find a Maushiro in an open area on the island.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: You must be speaking of the ceremonial site...

response.speaker: Ryuuji
response.text: As for the details, I no longer remember them well.

response.speaker: Ryuuji
response.text: Every time I try to do so, it's as if there's a fog in my head that prevents me from remembering the details of what occurred on Tsurumi Island.

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: Could it be that the fog that shrouds the island found its way into Ryuuji's head after he breathed too much of it in?

response.speaker: Roald
response.text: Well, here's what I experienced. At the time, I was trapped on Ritou with no way to cross the checkpoints.

response.speaker: Roald
response.text: This was when Miss Sumida contacted me and commissioned me to help her "go to Tsurumi Island to gather reference material and look for a Maushiro."

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So you don't have a permit, Mr. Roald?

response.speaker: Roald
response.text: Shh...! Come on now, these... less than legal dealings need not be spoken of so loudly.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Kama's really something, huh?

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: As long as it's asked of him, Kama will get it done.

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: But if you don't ask him, he won't do anything.

response.speaker: Roald
response.text: Like Ryuuji, I fear that I can't remember much about what occurred.

response.speaker: Roald
response.text: I took Kama's advice and walked through a large gateway into the fog... and I met a friendly child. There was... some sort of ceremony as well.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: A kid, you say... Was his name Ruu?

response.speaker: Roald
response.text: Ruu...? I don't quite remember. We did make the trip in a hurry, after all. Why, I even left my diary behind in Ritou.

response.speaker: Roald
response.text: The records clearly state that what civilization once existed on Tsurumi Island has been utterly destroyed, and yet there was still a child there.

response.speaker: Roald
response.text: I could've sworn that after a few other hurdles, I did finally get my hands on a Maushiro.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: "Could've sworn"?

response.speaker: Sango
response.text: Well, it does seem that Roald reported back to Sumida convinced that he had brought the item in question, while the truth was that he didn't have it. "Could've sworn" does seem to be the operative phrase here.

response.speaker: Roald
response.text: I'm very sorry. That's why I write diaries, you know? To compensate for my untrustworthy memory.

response.speaker: Roald
response.text: Well, I say that, but I do often lose those very diaries as well. So there you go...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: (Huh. You know what? We've discovered quite a lot of journals and diaries out in the wild. Does that mean that there's a ton of people with poor memories out there in the world?)

response.speaker: Sango
response.text: To be honest with you, what concerns me the most about these incidents isn't the missing Maushiro, but the fact that you met locals on Tsurumi Island at all.

response.speaker: Sango
response.text: According to the "Tales of Distant Seas," there can be no doubt that Tsurumi Island was utterly destroyed several millennia ago.

response.speaker: Sango
response.text: The monstrous bird of thunder was slain by the Electro Archon upon Amakumo Peak in Seirai Island. That was why the Asase Shrine was built — to suppress the leftover power of that giant bird.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait... Is this the Thunderbird we've heard about in the past?

response.speaker: Ryuuji
response.text: President Sango, this doesn't have anything to do with the case...

response.speaker: Sango
response.text: No, it does. Although I've never gone to Seirai myself, the fallout from the Thunderbird's death resulted in the strange phenomena that can be found on Amakumo Peak. When you add this together with the existence of ley line disorders, which have since become common knowledge as well...

response.speaker: Sango
response.text: Only one conclusion remains, and thus it must be true — that the strange occurrences that you experienced must be related to Tsurumi Island itself!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh...

choices.text: You know, this is all very fascinating...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But it won't be of any help!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You really do know a lot, Sango!

response.speaker: Sango
response.text: Of course, I am Sango of Bantan Sango Detective Agency, after all. If you wish to take on matters of all sorts, then you must have knowledge of all sorts.

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: Hmm... I do also feel that this gathering hasn't resulted in any meaningful conclusions, though...

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: Other than Mr. Roald and Bantan Sango, all the others I contacted believe that Tsurumi Island has some unique ley line disorder, or that it might even be haunted. None of them were willing to involve themselves any further.

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: Perhaps I should take the commission back. *sigh* Maybe the writer's life is not my destiny after all...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: No, that won't do!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: After hearing you say so much about "The Chronicles of the Sea of Fog," Miss Sumida, Paimon's now very, very curious to know what happens next!

response.speaker: Sango
response.text: As a detective, I do not believe in such things as "destiny."

response.speaker: Sango
response.text: Everything happens for a reason, and all occurrences follow their own unique logic. "Destiny" doesn't come into it at all.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: As long as we can find out what happened...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Then we can... Actually, you know what? What are we doing this for again?

choices.text: To encourage Miss Sumida, of course.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: No, that can't be it!

response.speaker: Roald
response.text: We're here to find the Maushiro and give it to Miss Sumida to finish the commission, aren't we?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's right! If she cancels the commission now, we'd have run around the whole place for nothing!

choices.text: That's the most important bit, huh?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, just leave it all to us, Miss Sumida!

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: Hmm... You're right. It's early days yet to be giving up.

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: Even the great Takizawa Kyouden muddled through life for thirty-three years before he read the...

response.speaker: Ryuuji
response.text: Miss Sumida, you're welcome to share your writing anecdotes next time you commission us. But for now, we shall take our leave.

response.speaker: Sango
response.text: Yup, I'm tired. Bantan Sango's courtyard is still the best.

response.speaker: Roald
response.text: #And as an adventurer, I feel obligated to challenge the fog over Tsurumi Island once more. Well then, let us meet again in the island's depths, {NICKNAME}. Ad astra abyssosque!

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: Looks like I need to improve my social skills on top of my writing ones, huh...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Aw, cheer up! Don't worry about the whole Maushiro thing. We'll get it done!

choices.text: That's what you think is most important, eh, Paimon?
I'm also very concerned about what's happening on Tsurumi Island.
To find the Maushiro.
Well, this information isn't very helpful...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh, at least it's interesting. Right?

choices.text: Is to find the answer as to why the Maushiro would disappear.
So then, about Tsurumi Island...

dialogues.speaker: Sumida
dialogues.text: The Maushiro... It's the key to writing "The Chronicles of the Sea of Fog (Working Title)"...

dialogues.speaker: Ruu
dialogues.text: Ah...

dialogues.speaker: Ruu
dialogues.text: #It's you, {NICKNAME} — and Paimon too...

dialogues.speaker: Ruu
dialogues.text: You went missing earlier. I thought that you'd ended up like all the others...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Others, you say?

dialogues.speaker: Ruu
dialogues.text: That's right. I met other outlanders before as well. But they all went missing, and then they never came back.

dialogues.speaker: Ruu
dialogues.text: There was a man in green, and another guy who called himself a "detective"... I wonder what's happened to all of them...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh, those people sure sound like Roald and Ryuuji, don't they?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: They're both fine.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We met them both just a while back!

dialogues.speaker: Ruu
dialogues.text: That's good... I was afraid that they'd gotten lost in the fog or gotten eaten by those monsters that look like dogs...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Nah, that won't happen! They've got the skills, y'know? Well, sorta.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Still, we did encounter a whole lotta weird stuff after splitting up with you, Ruu...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We don't know where the Maushiro we found's gone either.

dialogues.speaker: Ruu
dialogues.text: The Maushiro? You should still have it on you, I think. I can feel its power on you.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What?

dialogues.speaker: Ruu
dialogues.text: I once heard Grandpa Mata say...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...So the Thunderbird's feathers were the original "Maushiro"?

dialogues.speaker: Ruu
dialogues.text: That's right. I can feel that same sort of... power from you, I guess?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh, speaking of feathers, Paimon's reminded of something...

choices.text: Back at Amakumo Peak...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ohh, that's right! That did happen.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? Looks like something's shining...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wow...

choices.text: That's pretty amazing.

response.speaker: Ruu
response.text: Yup. These feathers are the best kind of Maushiro around.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That said, Paimon doesn't think this is what Miss Sumida's looking for...

response.speaker: Ruu
response.text: Man-made Maushiro do not have this kind of power, but since this is the "original form" of such Maushiro, it should have some special abilities. Perhaps it can even see the spirits of the dead.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's kinda hard to believe — well, Paimon says that, but we've done all kinds of weird stuff many times before anyway...

response.speaker: Ruu
response.text: Let's try using it!

choices.text: That's kinda spooky.
The commission to Seirai Island...

talks.objective: Go to your destination and use the feather

dialogues.speaker: Mata
dialogues.text: I hope that... No, the Great Thunderbird will surely be pleased with the ceremony this time...

dialogues.speaker: Mata
dialogues.text: After all, this is the only child that she has shown favor to in all these years...

dialogues.speaker: Chise
dialogues.text: Eminent Priest, Ruu has yet to arrive.

dialogues.speaker: Mata
dialogues.text: ...This is the final day. Let him wander for a little while longer.

dialogues.speaker: Chise
dialogues.text: But the Great Thunderbird has already returned to Mt. Kanna!

dialogues.speaker: Mata
dialogues.text: Is that so? Then truly, our time is limited...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Is there anything we can help with? Ruu's our friend.

dialogues.speaker: Mata
dialogues.text: Well then. Wakukau, Oina, Autake...

dialogues.speaker: Mata
dialogues.text: Please look for him in these places. I believe that you might find him there.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Leave it to us! We'll find Ruu for sure!

dialogues.speaker: Chise
dialogues.text: Wakukau Shoal, Oina Beach, and Autake Plains...

dialogues.speaker: Chise
dialogues.text: Forgive my forwardness, but I do not think these are places where a child should go...

dialogues.speaker: Mata
dialogues.text: That is true. But these are his favorite spots.

dialogues.speaker: Chise
dialogues.text: It was at Autake Plains that Ruu encountered the Great Thunderbird, wasn't it?

dialogues.speaker: Mata
dialogues.text: Yes. When we were together, he would often talk about the times he went fishing with Ipe by the shore at Wakukau, and how he would pick seashells at Oina with Sayo and the Kama family's boy.

dialogues.speaker: Chise
dialogues.text: Sayo... That loudmouth. She always talks about the world outside the Sea of Fog. We should've left her outside the fog with nothing but three days' rations, just like our forebears used to do.

dialogues.speaker: Chise
dialogues.text: If we had, Kama wouldn't have ended up like that, either...

dialogues.speaker: Mata
dialogues.text: This is all past tense now. There's nothing more to be said.

dialogues.speaker: Mata
dialogues.text: I must continue making preparations for the Thunderbird's descent. I leave the rest to you.

dialogues.speaker: Chise
dialogues.text: As you wish.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uhh, Paimon's getting nervous... It's like that time with Dusky Ming...

choices.text: Dusky Ming wasn't a bad girl.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh. You're right. Paimon's sorry, Dusky Ming!

response.speaker: Ruu
response.text: Ah, it's Big Brother Kama. I wonder how he's doing now.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Eh? Kama?

choices.text: Well, then we've got nothing to be afraid of, right?

dialogues.speaker: "Kama"
dialogues.text: ...I'll bury this here. This is where we met each other, after all.

dialogues.speaker: "Kama"
dialogues.text: I'll leave the Maushiro that I couldn't pass to you then over here.

dialogues.speaker: "Kama"
dialogues.text: If I wish to bid this... whatever this place is, farewell, I can't bring anything with me — that's what you told me before you left.

dialogues.speaker: Ruu
dialogues.text: *sigh* So he's left Tsurumi Island already...

dialogues.speaker: Ruu
dialogues.text: I hope he's doing alright...

dialogues.speaker: Ruu
dialogues.text: Well! Today's the day of the ceremony, so we shouldn't dwell on unhappy things!

dialogues.speaker: Ruu
dialogues.text: I've made an agreement with Kapatcir that I'll go see her soon. Everyone's going to help me get ready, too, so I've gotta go.

dialogues.speaker: Ruu
dialogues.text: Thanks for helping me out with the Perches! With your help, the ceremony is sure to go great this time!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hehe, of course!

dialogues.speaker: Ruu
dialogues.text: Hmm... If you don't mind, could you help me look for Grandpa Mata at the ceremonial site?

dialogues.speaker: Ruu
dialogues.text: Even though our perch problem has been solved, there are other things we need help with. The ceremony is a very important event, after all. Lots of preparations need to be done first.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh, is that so? The last time we went to make an offering at the Perch, he was gone.

dialogues.speaker: Ruu
dialogues.text: Gone? No, this is such an important ceremony. There's no way he'd leave it half done. I mean...

dialogues.speaker: Ruu
dialogues.text: Ah, it's nothing. In any case, please help me out!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #*sigh* What do you think, {NICKNAME}?

choices.text: Sure.

response.speaker: Ruu
response.text: Thanks, you two!

response.speaker: Ruu
response.text: Well then, let's meet again later!

choices.text: I'm fine with it.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: This... This is...

choices.text: This is the Maushiro.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh... Does that mean that the commission's complete?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Probably.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Anyway, since we gave Ruu our word, let's head over to the ceremonial site and have a look.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: No take-backsies with kids, remember? Paimon doesn't wanna become a lousy adult!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: You count as an adult?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, compared to being a kid, Paimon sure is closer to being an adult...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I mean, Dusky Ming's a kid, but she's pretty old, you know?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ugh, counting's hard. Let's just skip the details, shall we?

choices.text: Well, it's easier to carry than before, that's for sure.

dialogues.speaker: Kito
dialogues.text: ...That's just weird. And the priests on the drawings up there don't look like Grandpa Mata or the others at all.

dialogues.speaker: Kina
dialogues.text: Yeah, it's super weird!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey there!

dialogues.speaker: Kito
dialogues.text: I've got a guess!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: They're not paying us any mind at all! Paimon's gonna get mad!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We might as well listen in...

dialogues.speaker: Kina
dialogues.text: Hah, it's time for Big Brother Kito's wild guesses! Alright, what've you got this time?

dialogues.speaker: Kito
dialogues.text: These murals depict a time before the Sea of Fog. A long, long time ago, there was no fog over the world, so everyone could see what was up there!

dialogues.speaker: Kito
dialogues.text: Up there, they could see these round- and pointy-shaped things, and these mountain-like things! That's why these ancient murals look the way they do!

dialogues.speaker: Kina
dialogues.text: That's some imagination you've got there, Kito!

dialogues.speaker: Kito
dialogues.text: Hehe.

dialogues.speaker: Kina
dialogues.text: But not a word of this to Grandpa Mata or Granny Una! We'll be in for an earful otherwise...

dialogues.speaker: Kito
dialogues.text: Yup, I know!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: "Round- and pointy-shaped things"... Are they talking about the moon and stars depicted here on the mural? The fog's so thick here, it's no wonder that they couldn't see 'em.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So the children of Tsurumi Island thought this way, huh. Paimon wonders what else they believed?

talks.objective: Listen in on the locals' conversations

dialogues.speaker: "Ipe"
dialogues.text: ...Oh, this? Well, the secret to fishing is patience.

dialogues.speaker: "Ipe"
dialogues.text: No, no, it's not boring at all. I love fishing.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: He sounds like he's talking to someone.

dialogues.speaker: "Ipe"
dialogues.text: The fish don't sing, but if you sing to them, I'm sure they can hear you.

dialogues.speaker: "Ipe"
dialogues.text: Not that this means they wouldn't eat you too, of course!

dialogues.speaker: "Ipe"
dialogues.text: No problem. Once you're older, I'll teach you how to fish.

dialogues.speaker: "Ipe"
dialogues.text: But when you grow up, you've got to teach me the secret of the Ishine Script. I mean, this is knowledge that only gets passed through the priestly families — you know, your family.

dialogues.speaker: "Ipe"
dialogues.text: For example, the words on those rocks...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm, looks like we've gotta go look for Ruu again, huh?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: According to what they said earlier, Ruu could be at Wakukau Shoal, Oina Beach, or the Autake Plains...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ugh, why are all these names so annoying to remember...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: The location closest to us is...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Seems like it should be Wakukau Shoal, right?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well then, guess that's where we're starting!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon feels cheated, though. Ruu asked us to come here, and now the people here want us to look for him.

choices.text: Maybe we can better understand the island this way.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Well, if you say so, {NICKNAME}, let's do it!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We've got the Maushiro already anyway... As long as it doesn't disappear for no reason again.

choices.text: Who knows, Paimon? There might be treasure.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow! It appeared!

dialogues.speaker: "Ipe"
dialogues.text: Huh, to think that Ishine Script had this kind of power. Perhaps it's related to the ley lines in some way... How unexpected.

dialogues.speaker: "Ipe"
dialogues.text: You're right. The previous priests did have a sense of humor, huh?

dialogues.speaker: "Ipe"
dialogues.text: ...Why do I like fishing? Hmm, let me think about it for a moment...

dialogues.speaker: "Ipe"
dialogues.text: If I had to put my finger on it, it's because fishing makes me feel like this ocean and the rest of the world are connected. That way, this island doesn't feel so small, even though we can't escape the Sea of Fog.

dialogues.speaker: "Ipe"
dialogues.text: And... Uh, how should I say this? I guess I've also fished up all kinds of interesting stuff along the way.

dialogues.speaker: "Ipe"
dialogues.text: Like for example, the knowledge that you love to sing in secret.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, is he talking to Ruu?

choices.text: Well, if people can talk to dragons...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Th—That's true, yeah... We've really seen a lot of weird stuff while traveling together, huh?

response.speaker: "Ipe"
response.text: C'mon, it's nothing to be embarrassed about. You sing pretty well! I feel luckier just listening to you, you know?

response.speaker: "Ipe"
response.text: You wanna sing for Makiri? Sure, but I mean, why d'you need to ask me?

response.speaker: "Ipe"
response.text: Alright then. If you're going to Oina Beach, say hi to Kama and the others for me.

response.speaker: "Ipe"
response.text: Careful now, if you get lost in the fog, just play the Maushiro. I'll come find you for sure.

choices.text: Then the ability to talk to nonexistent people isn't too strange.

talks.objective: Use the feather to search for clues
Solve the mystery of the stones

dialogues.speaker: "Sayo"
dialogues.text: You know, Ruu...

dialogues.speaker: "Sayo"
dialogues.text: Would you like to come with me?

dialogues.speaker: "Sayo"
dialogues.text: I'm serious! The world outside this fog really does exist!

dialogues.speaker: "Sayo"
dialogues.text: I've seen people come in from the outside. Once, there was someone who came to the island, lost their way in the fog, and injured themselves in a fall as a result.

dialogues.speaker: "Sayo"
dialogues.text: That person told me all sorts of things about the outside world. He said that he came from an island on the other side of the sea. There's no fog there — only rolling green lands, a blue sky, and a golden sun.

dialogues.speaker: "Sayo"
dialogues.text: He said that the Thunderbird always flies from our island to his, and it was the sight of the Thunderbird in flight that made him want to come over and see what it's like here.

dialogues.speaker: "Sayo"
dialogues.text: I know, right? I found it really mysterious, too!

dialogues.speaker: "Sayo"
dialogues.text: So how about it, then? Wanna come with me? This place is just too stifling.

dialogues.speaker: "Sayo"
dialogues.text: Grandpa Mata isn't a bad person, but he just isn't willing to doubt our ancestors' words. But as for me, I want to go see what the outside world is like!

dialogues.speaker: "Sayo"
dialogues.text: Anyway, I hate the idea of offering people to the Thunderbird... And I'm sure the Thunderbird probably hates it too.

dialogues.speaker: "Sayo"
dialogues.text: Well, about Kama... That's true, huh. If we left him alone here...

dialogues.speaker: "Sayo"
dialogues.text: But I get it. If you've decided to stay, then I'm sure this place will become a better one thanks to you!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh, it's Ruu!

dialogues.speaker: "Ruu"
dialogues.text: If I sing here, no one will discover me, right...?

dialogues.speaker: "Ruu"
dialogues.text: Hmm... Maybe I should go deeper inside!

talks.objective: Use the feather to search for clues

dialogues.speaker: "Sayo"
dialogues.text: Hey there.

dialogues.speaker: "Kama"
dialogues.text: Oh, it's you, Ruu.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh, that's the weird "Kama" from before...

dialogues.speaker: "Sayo"
dialogues.text: Sorry to disappoint you, but I've picked every last seashell off this beach today!

dialogues.speaker: "Kama"
dialogues.text: I mean, wasn't our intention to give them to him so—

dialogues.speaker: "Sayo"
dialogues.text: Hey!

dialogues.speaker: "Kama"
dialogues.text: Ah.

dialogues.speaker: "Sayo"
dialogues.text: Hehe, maybe I should say instead that you've come at just the right time.

dialogues.speaker: "Sayo"
dialogues.text: I mean, aren't there some rocks with that... Uh, whatever you call that writing again, on them.

dialogues.speaker: "Sayo"
dialogues.text: I remember you saying that the order was very important, Ruu. So if we mess the rocks' order up...

dialogues.speaker: "Kama"
dialogues.text: They call it the Ishine Script. I've said this before, I don't think this is a good idea.

dialogues.speaker: "Kama"
dialogues.text: And Ruu's here too. I don't think he'll let us do this, considering that he's the son of the priest and all...

dialogues.speaker: "Kama"
dialogues.text: What? You wanna join in?

dialogues.speaker: "Sayo"
dialogues.text: Hah! See? I always knew Ruu wasn't some stick-in-the-mud!

dialogues.speaker: "Sayo"
dialogues.text: Alright then, let's do this!

dialogues.speaker: "Sayo"
dialogues.text: Hahaha, this is real funny, watching a future priest touch these stones just like the records say they should... and then coming up blank in the end.

dialogues.speaker: "Kama"
dialogues.text: I still think this isn't right.

dialogues.speaker: "Sayo"
dialogues.text: Pfft, this guy's a bore. You know what? Let's not hang out with him. Let's go ruin-delving with Kito and Kina!

dialogues.speaker: "Kama"
dialogues.text: Actually, Ruu, since you're pretty friendly with those two, could you remind them to please take care of themselves?

dialogues.speaker: "Kama"
dialogues.text: I, too, believe that there are green lands beyond the Sea of Fog, and humans too, and that there were people and history before the Thunderbird came, but someone needs to record the things that happened in our village.

dialogues.speaker: "Sayo"
dialogues.text: Tch. You're such a killjoy.

dialogues.speaker: "Sayo"
dialogues.text: You know what, Ruu? You should grow older faster.

dialogues.speaker: "Sayo"
dialogues.text: If you were the priest, I'm sure you'd lead us all out of the Sea of Fog to see the outside world...

dialogues.speaker: "Sayo"
dialogues.text: I wonder, can I wait for that day to come?

dialogues.speaker: "Sayo"
dialogues.text: Ah, right. Kama said that he saw you at the Autake Plains the other day.

dialogues.speaker: "Sayo"
dialogues.text: You've gotta be careful over there. The fog is thickest in that area — you fall off the cliff and that's the end for you!

dialogues.speaker: "Kama"
dialogues.text: Mm. If you really do have to go, take me with you.

dialogues.speaker: "Sayo"
dialogues.text: That's right! Kama over here's got a brain like a rock, but he's no ordinary rock — he's got a sense of direction!

talks.objective: Restore the stones and solve the puzzle

dialogues.speaker: Sumida
dialogues.text: I need to reflect on how I speak to people...

talks.objective: Use the feather to search for clues

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Everyone's gone...

choices.text: Well, what was I expecting...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We've met bake-danuki on the other islands before... Could this all be a big trick of theirs!?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ooh, now Paimon's getting angry!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Let's take stock of the situation first, shall we?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, of course!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: If we have to keep trudging through all this cloud and fog, it had better be worth it!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: So we got the Maushiro.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Even though we don't know if it'll disappear or not...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hopefully, we can get it back to Miss Sumida this time!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: There's a person here who looks a lot like Kama...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: He looks like him and he's also got the name to match. Very suspicious...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Time passes strangely on Tsurumi Island...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm. Now that you mention it...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: When we spoke to Ruu, it felt really weird, like time was passing differently for him and us...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh! Right, and he met Ryuuji and Roald, didn't he?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: The people here can't seem to see us.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Is that so? Hmm, Paimon did get a weird feeling as well when we tried talking to them.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: They didn't even look at us at all! So rude!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...That's all, right?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ugh, thinking is so tiring.

choices.text: I was the only one doing the thinking, though.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's not true! Paimon tried her best!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yup, let's go back and look for Miss Sumida.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: If we meet Kama along the way, let's ask him some questions as well.

choices.text: Well, let's head back first.
There's no further meaning in staying here.
I suppose this was to be expected.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Ooh, looks like there's another Thunderbird statue here. C'mon, {NICKNAME}, let's give our feather a try!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: There seem to be some missing stones over there... Let's find the matching stones and return them to their places. That should be the ticket!

talks.objective: Use the feather to search for clues
Return the stones to their rightful place

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ah, wait a moment.

choices.text: Right, we need to check real quick...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yup! We've gotta make sure that we've still got that Maushiro.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: If not, this trip is gonna be a wash as well!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Phew, that's great! It didn't go missing this time.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Alrighty then! Back to Miss Sumida's we go!

choices.text: What's up?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We've gotta make sure that we've still got that Maushiro, of course!

talks.objective: Solve the mystery of the stones

dialogues.text: Curious tunes, tiny human. Afraid not of thunder and storms?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ruu seems to be talking to someone...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ah, he's gone...

dialogues.speaker: Sumida
dialogues.text: Oh, you're back.

dialogues.speaker: Sumida
dialogues.text: I really hope you've brought the Maushiro this time... Or else...

dialogues.speaker: Sumida
dialogues.text: ...Or else my novel will never get written!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, come on! A commission of this level was a piece of cake for us!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #C'mon, {NICKNAME}, let's show her the Maushiro we found!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Let's finish this commission, get paid, and head over to Kiminami Restaurant for a good meal...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...Wait a moment.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon feels like she's had this conversation before. Is it just Paimon's imagination?

choices.text: The Maushiro...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: And it's good that it is, too!

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: I... Is this it? Is this how I, Sumida, will obtain the Maushiro?

choices.text: Is in my hands!

dialogues.speaker: Sumida
dialogues.text: Ahh... So this is a Maushiro?

dialogues.speaker: Sumida
dialogues.text: You know, I can't help but feel a bit disappointed.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Eh!?

choices.text: Huh?

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: Ah, I'm sorry. I'm just thinking that it lacks, you know, that sense of destiny.

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: This is an artifact retrieved from the wreckage of a civilization from which no laughter or song has been heard for thousands of years. To think that I would get my hands on it so easily...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's right! It took a lot of effort for us to get this! Don't you make it out to be some simple matter!

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: S—Sorry!

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: #A—As expected of the legendary {NICKNAME}...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: And what about Paimon, huh?

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: And the renowned Paimon!

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: I mean, you completed a commission that even famed adventurers and detectives could not, and so smoothly at that!

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: #Impressive! Yes, very impressive! You know, I was even thinking of changing the name of my novel from "The Chronicles of the Sea of Fog" to the "The Tales of {NICKNAME} and Paimon!"

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: #Hmm, {NICKNAME} and Paimon, Paimon and {NICKNAME}... It doesn't feel like it rolls off the tongue very well. I think my editor might reject it...

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: Oh, I know! Why don't you change your names to "Fog" and "Sea" respectively?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Eh?

choices.text: What?

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: Uh, hahahaha, I was kidding, just kidding! I mean, getting back on topic, even highly-experienced outlander mercenaries couldn't get this Maushiro. It's just absolutely amazing that it came into your hands this way.

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: Hmm, even "Shinzen," widely regarded as the strongest character in "The Three Young Nobles," would be no match for you.

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: Of course, a small minority believe that "Hakushuusai" is stronger still, but if they read the work preceding that, "The Prison Official"...

choices.text: Ugh, please, spare me the flattery.

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: ...I suppose.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You suppose?

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: Well... Truth be told, I'd like to hear about your adventures on Tsurumi Island.

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: It must have taken some twists and turns for you to get a hold of the Maushiro, right? I'm sure that some of those parts might be worth writing about...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Actually, we've got some questions that we'd like to discuss as well...

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: Huh, is that how it is...

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: Even though Tsurumi Island has already been destroyed, certain people and periods of time will play back at abnormal speeds, just like wraiths might. Not to mention how the passage of time within the fog is very different from how it might pass in the outside world.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: We haven't actually talked about that yet...

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: But those people are not ghosts in the traditional sense, but are instead "occurrences" being replayed over and over, and so they do not notice the visiting protagonist. Amidst all this, a mysterious boy...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: The "protagonist"?

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: So those who took the commission in the past could not retrieve the Maushiro because they received a fake "Ghost Maushiro" instead.

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: I see. So that's how it is. I understand now.

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: Hmm, you know what? I think you two have some writing talent!

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: This is very interesting indeed, but some aspects of this story are quite rigid and unconducive to the development of the setting. Still...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: "Setting"? What's that?

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: Oh, don't worry about it. I think that with some time and some polish, this story will definitely sell well!

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: Aratani should like this sort of story, too. Maybe I'll even get a contract with Yae Publishing House!

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: Ahh, my days of professional writing are coming soon, aren't they... No, no, I haven't even decided on a pen name yet. Or maybe using my real name like Mr. Nine does might be cooler...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Sumida's been mumbling all kinds of gibberish for a while now. Is she alright...?

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: ...That's right, my commission isn't over just yet.

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: Whether true or false, I still require more stories concerning Tsurumi Island...

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: ...A—And if possible, I'd like to know more about him... About Kama, that is.

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: I—I mean, he is my reliable partner, isn't he? We've sailed through wild storms, just like the legendary Ako Domeki Zaemon and Janome Gonbei...

choices.text: You mean the time you almost died?

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: ...Uh, well, the legends do say that Ako Domeki was saved by Janome many times.

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: In any case, I want to learn more about Kama.

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: I—I mean, he's just got that "keeping his true power a mystery, only to join the protagonist's party in the closing phases of the story" feel to him, you know? I think it'll be well worth writing such a character into the plot.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: He certainly is very mysterious...

choices.text: I accept your commission.

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: Thank you...!

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: Well then, please continue your exploration of Tsurumi Island...

choices.text: I'd like to explore Tsurumi Island further as well.
You mean the time you threw up some purple goop?
Well, is the commission complete, then?
You're really annoying, you know that?
If you're not satisfied, you can go to Tsurumi Island yourself.
What?

dialogues.speaker: Kito
dialogues.text: Hmm. You know what? I have another guess.

dialogues.speaker: Kina
dialogues.text: Ooh, look at you, Big Brother Kito, you've got two guesses in a row!

dialogues.speaker: Kito
dialogues.text: Shh... Shh!

dialogues.speaker: Kito
dialogues.text: (I wonder... Does Grandpa Mata also not know about what happened so long ago?)

dialogues.speaker: Kina
dialogues.text: (Wow! Now that's an exciting thought.)

dialogues.speaker: Kito
dialogues.text: (Just think about it, Kina... He said that a long, long time ago, when the darkness fell, the Great Thunderbird protected us using the Sea of Fog.)

dialogues.speaker: Kito
dialogues.text: (But if it was that long ago , Grandpa can't have seen that for himself, whether it be the sights up there, or the outside world itself...)

dialogues.speaker: Kito
dialogues.text: (I think that even the belief that the Great Thunderbird is protecting us with this fog might be fake!)

dialogues.speaker: Kina
dialogues.text: (That's mighty bold of you, Kito! But... you might be right!)
